title: Gold Retreats From Record Highs as Jewellers Bet on Diwali Demand
excerpt: Prices are down nearly 20% from the January record to Rs 14,315 per gram, but IBJA expects October volumes to fall 11% year on year as lightweight designs and old-gold exchange sustain value sales ahead of Dhanteras and Diwali.
body:
• Gold has retreated nearly 20% from its record of Rs 17,885 per gram on January 30, 2026, to Rs 14,315 per gram for 24-carat on October 22, according to the India Bullion and Jewellers Association.
  • Retail prices were still high in absolute terms — about Rs 1,43,447 per 10 grams on October 22 — and the IBJA expects October gold sales volumes to fall 11% year on year despite festive buying.
  • Value sales are holding up better than volumes: listed jewellers grew revenue 20-30% in July-September, and old-gold exchanges accounted for over 50% of sales at some retailers.
  • For buyers ahead of Dhanteras and Diwali in November, the practical takeaway is price, not timing: at Rs 14,315 per gram plus making charges and 3% GST, lightweight designs and old-gold exchange are how most shoppers are keeping budgets intact.

A correction, not a collapse

Gold prices have retreated from record highs ahead of the peak festive season, giving jewellers a mixed picture: healthier footfall and value sales, but cautious volumes as buyers adjust to prices that remain far above last Diwali.

According to the India Bullion and Jewellers Association (IBJA), 24-carat gold stood at Rs 14,315 per gram on October 22, with 22-carat at Rs 13,113 per gram, 18-carat at Rs 10,736 and 14-carat at Rs 8,374, Outlook Money reported from the World Gold Council's latest India market update. That is down nearly 20% from the record Rs 17,885 per gram on January 30, 2026.

In the terms most retail buyers see, gold traded at Rs 1,43,447 per 10 grams on October 22, and the polled spot price in Ahmedabad was Rs 1,43,430 per 10 grams, according to reporting of the Moneycontrol story by Informist.

"Manufacturers are reporting healthy order flows as retailers replenish inventories to meet this seasonal demand, while industry feedback points to improving in-store footfall."

— World Gold Council, India gold market update

Volumes down, value up

Surendra Mehta, secretary of the IBJA, expects October gold sales to fall 11% year on year in volume, even though purchases are higher than in September, the Moneycontrol report said. Mehta does not expect a significant recovery in demand in the coming weeks, and jewellery shares reacted on October 22, with Kalyan Jewellers down nearly 5%, Senco Gold down over 3% and Titan down over 1%.

The World Gold Council picture is more nuanced. Listed jewellery retailers reported revenue growth of 20-30% year on year in the July-September quarter despite a less favourable festive calendar, Outlook Money reported. Higher prices lift the value of each sale even when the weight sold falls.

Two adaptations explain the resilience. First, buyers are choosing lightweight jewellery. Second, old-gold exchange has become a core sales driver: exchange transactions rose more than 10% year on year and accounted for over 50% of sales at some retailers. Senco Gold reported 29% retail revenue growth in Q2 FY27 and said exchanges were over 50% of its sales, while PC Jeweller reported sales up 28% to Rs 1,054 crore.

What is driving prices

The near-term trend remains weak, the Moneycontrol report noted, with a stronger rupee and inflation concerns weighing on prices and the US Federal Reserve's October 28 policy decision in focus. The detailed market data is tracked by the World Gold Council update reported by Outlook Money.

India's gold imports tell the same cautious story. Imports fell to $1.8 billion in September, the lowest since March 2024, down 22% from August and 81% year on year to an estimated 20 tonnes, partly because recycled gold from exchange programmes increased domestic availability.

What to watch for Diwali

Dhanteras, Diwali and Bhai Dooj fall in November this year, after Navratri, Dussehra and Durga Puja concluded in October. Retailers have ramped up campaigns, exchange schemes, flexible payment options and gold-rate protection on advance payments.

The festive test is whether the roughly 20% correction from the record is enough to bring volume buyers back, or whether value growth continues to mask lighter baskets. For now, jewellers are planning for healthy sales in rupees, not in grams.
